summary.headline: Fine Organic FY26 consolidated revenue rose 4.3% to INR 2,365 crore and PAT 1.6% to INR 417 crore; management guides flat growth until SEZ commissioning in 2H FY28.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 4.3% to INR 2,365 crore from INR 2,269 crore, with PAT up 1.6% to INR 417 crore and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. Management said all plants run at near full utilisation, so volume growth is capped until the JNPA SEZ plant and US plant come on line. The company approved acquiring up to 80% of Oleofine Organics BHD, Malaysia (cash consideration about INR 82.9 crore), and continued capex in SEZ, US, Dubai and Thailand. Raw material and freight costs rose in Q4 on the West Asia conflict, and management expects vegetable-oil prices to stay high through FY27.

financial_highlights.change: excluded from underlying employee cost growth of about 15% cited by analyst

financial_highlights.value: INR 18 crore in Q4 vs INR 14 crore in Q3
financial_highlights.change: about +25% QoQ; management attributed part to Ind AS lease adjustments

segments.name: Specialty additives (food, plastics, polymers, feed nutrition, personal care, coatings, inks, rubber)
segments.commentary: All manufacturing facilities run at almost full utilisation. Feed nutrition now has 14-15 commercialised products. Products are used at 0.1%-0.5% dosage as performance additives.

segments.name: Oleofine Organics BHD (Malaysia, food additives, palm-based)
segments.commentary: Turnover about MYR 23.3 million, about INR 54 crore as of 31 Jan 2026 (transcript note corrects an earlier INR 44 crore figure). Acquisition of up to 80%: 50% from promoter-group entity Smoothex Chemicals, 30% from other shareholders, for about MYR 34.2 million (about INR 82.9 crore).

guidance_outlook: FY27 and FY28 expected to be flat in top line until SEZ plant commissioning; any top-line increase will come from price, not volume.
JNPA SEZ plant: commercial production expected in 2H FY28; total investment INR 700-750 crore, with the bulk in Phase 1 capex.
US plant (South Carolina, 160 acres): construction not yet started; commissioning in 18-24 months from construction start, targeting 18 months; investment figure to be announced next quarter.
EBITDA margin sustainable at 18%-20%, per management's view based on the last 10 years.
Raw material prices expected to stay elevated through FY27, especially vegetable oils; employee cost increase in FY27 expected to be similar to FY26 (excluding the one-time INR 7 crore).
Oleofine acquisition expected to close within about 3 months, subject to approvals and definitive agreements.
capex_capacity: SEZ (JNPA) project in Fine Organic Industries (SEZ) Private Limited: INR 65 crore preference share infusion in FY26; total investment in the subsidiary about INR 192.5 crore to date; commercial production expected 2H FY28; initial exports to transfer products from Ambernath.

US subsidiary (100% owned): about USD 1.12 million (about INR 9.6 crore) equity infused; about 160 acres acquired in Jonesville, Union County, South Carolina; Phase 1 deliberately conservative capacity, with at least 3 phases planned; capacity figures withheld.
Patalganga facility (food additives) in steady ramp-up; expected to reach full capacity in FY27.
Thailand JV: equity increased by about INR 6.17 crore (THB 22.5 million) in FY26; plant at full scale, expansion deferred a few months until SEZ team is free.
Dubai subsidiary (GCC presence): equity of AED 2 lakh (about INR 49.5 lakh) infused in Q4 FY26.
Malaysia (OFM): existing land deemed sufficient to start; expansion planned into palm and palm-kernel-based specialty products.
demand_pricing: Management sees no change in demand; customers in the Middle East face port disruptions, and customers have agreed to buy on FOB terms, taking on extra freight costs.
Contracting is now short-term (1-3 months) because of raw material volatility; the company is not signing long-term contracts.
Palm oil supply is tightening due to Indonesian biodiesel mandates (B50) and Malaysian blending; management expects palm and other vegetable oil prices to keep rising until the conflict ends.
Ammonia: no disruption so far, supported by storage and supplier tie-ups; risk if conflict prolongs.
Domestic customers get priority in allocation during short supply; export customers are asked to buy less.
Management expects some domestic product approvals to be needed only for new products; global approvals already exist for most existing products.
Freight costs rose in Q4 FY26 due to West Asia disruptions.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation affecting demand and supply chains?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is stable. Middle East port disruptions raised freight, and customers accepted FOB terms. Palm oil prices are expected to keep rising until the conflict ends, and raw materials are not expected to fall in the near future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SEZ investment and the revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is about INR 700-750 crore, mostly in Phase 1 capex with some Phase 2 base. Management declined to give revenue potential, citing volatile prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the JNPA plant, and do product approvals need to be redone?
qa_highlights.answer: Start is expected in at least 2H FY28. Initial products are existing exports, so approvals are largely a formality; only 2-3 large customers (e.g., Japanese or US) may need a process audit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US plant delayed by policy, and how big is Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Local government is supportive; the 50% import duty was temporary and duty is now 10-15%, which management accepts. Phase 1 capacity was not disclosed; the first phase is kept conservative for initial operating issues.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Oleofine (Malaysia), a small business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it a strategic move for palm-based oleochemical derivatives, which India lacks. It plans a sizable expansion, starting with specialty products.

qa_highlights.question: Is ammonia supply a risk, and how does the outlook for FY27 look?
qa_highlights.answer: No ammonia disruption yet. Management expects some palm oil tightness and high vegetable oil prices throughout FY27, and it is watching the situation closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CWIP not risen meaningfully, and when will SEZ commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractors have been onboarded and advances released only recently; meaningful CWIP will show in coming quarters. Commissioning is expected in 2H FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY26 growth been low after 2022-23, and is 18%+ EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: 2022-23 was an exceptional year due to raw material stockpiling. Sustainable EBITDA is 18%-20%. Growth will stay flat until SEZ and US plants start, and FY27 is expected to be flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex phased rather than continuous?
qa_highlights.answer: A Gujarat land allotment in Dholera (about 100 acres) was withdrawn after more than a year, delaying expansion by 1-1.5 years.

risks_watch: SEZ commissioning slip beyond 2H FY28; the company has limited manpower because one team is handling SEZ, US, Thailand and Malaysia.
Palm and vegetable oil prices and supply tightness; FY27 raw material costs expected to stay high; short-term contracts limit pricing pass-through visibility.
Freight disruption from West Asia; FOB shifting risk to customers.
US plant: contractor contracts not finalised, capex figure not yet disclosed, and first-time US operations risk.
Oleofine acquisition closing within 3 months, integration, and the INR 54 crore revenue base versus INR 82.9 crore price; the company is not disclosing expected returns.
Rising employee costs (about 15% underlying growth in FY26, similar expected in FY27) and rising depreciation (Q4 INR 18 crore vs INR 14 crore in Q3).
CWIP build-up in coming quarters should confirm SEZ construction progress.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and sustainable margins, but cautious and guarded on the near term: management repeatedly said FY27 will be flat and refused to give US capacity, SEZ revenue, or Phase 1 figures. Confident in customer cooperation and the timelines, but many answers were qualitative.
